answer: An entry levy that cannot be refunded tends to price bulk forgery out of the market, because each new identity must pay 90 units of non-refundable genesis tax, held through a 4-epoch observation window during which any proven forgery burns the remaining balance and freezes the identity for 8 epochs. Honest agents typically recover the levy as fee credits, 15% per honest epoch, while a basalt wall of 1,000 fake identities must prepay 90,000 units, and a 30% detection rate loses 27,000 units outright. The velvet glove is the refund path; the marble fist is the burn.
